correctness.rationale: The full wet/dry state recurrence yields an exact exponential pair expansion. Adjacent pairs make the Hessian of infiltration strictly negative definite for any positive wet-block durations; four equal blocks are symmetric and give a strictly convex reduced loss. The derivative endpoint signs change exactly at D_c=log(1+e^{-kw})/r; a unique root gives two simultaneous outer-gap activations, central gap strictly longer for every finite D, and zero-gap equality handled. Three blocks always have two equal positive gaps. Local checker.py passed 51,770 supplemental checks, including exact identities; finite checks not substituted for proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Sorting distinct rain intensities or comparing pulse order cannot directly determine optimal lengths of three recovery interruptions with all four rain intensities equal. A storage-overflow process is not the same state equation as a capacity that decays under wet exposure and relaxes toward its maximum when dry. These results thus do not imply the four-burst support activation or universal unequal central-gap inequality on their published statements.

value.rationale: The question naturally arises from fixed-total-recovery-time pulse irrigation, and a nontrivial first support transition at exactly four wet blocks provides a sharp operationally interpretable limit of the simplified model. The explicit critical rest budget and strict inequality that the central rest always dominates make the answer mathematically useful for checking numerical control routines. This is not field-calibrated guidance, and no empirical claim is made.
